classification.difficultyReason: Carry out the same addition using two explicitly prescribed methods, supported by fraction bars, then state a personal preference without needing to discover or justify a new method.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Work out $1\frac{1}{6}+3\frac{3}{4}$ by converting each mixed number into an improper fraction.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 3a: paired fraction bars below the instruction
spec.description: Two rows of equal-sized whole bars. The upper row contains one complete sixths bar and one sixths bar with one shaded cell. The lower row contains three complete quarters bars and one quarters bar with three shaded cells.
spec.mathematics: The shaded regions represent 1 1/6 and 3 3/4; every whole has the same width.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied model; no calculated answer is embedded.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Work out $1\frac{1}{6}+3\frac{3}{4}$ by first adding the wholes and then adding the fractions.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 3b: paired fraction bars below the instruction
spec.description: Two rows of equal-sized whole bars. Complete whole bars are undivided. The upper row has one complete whole followed by one shaded sixth; the lower row has three complete wholes followed by three shaded quarters.
spec.mathematics: Undivided bars emphasise adding the four wholes separately from 1/6 and 3/4.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied model; no calculated answer is embedded.

answer.short: Answers vary. For example, the second method is a bit easier as you work with smaller numbers.
answer.worked: Either preference is acceptable. For example, the second method uses smaller numbers because the wholes and fractions are added separately.
